concepts.why: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall, demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement, suggests a neoplastic process.

The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion and an indistinct outline of the adjacent bladder wall, combined with a history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a left hydrosalpinx, suggests a possible diagnosis of bladder endometriosis.
The presence of tiny hyperechoic foci and a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall suggests a possible diagnosis of malacoplakia.
The presence of dysuria, hematuria, and pus cells in the urine suggests a possible diagnosis of urinary tract infection.
The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation suggests a possible diagnosis of nephrolithiasis.

rationales.F06: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the urinary bladder is highly suggestive of a neoplastic lesion, such as cancer.
rationales.F09: The well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall is highly indicative of a malignant tumor, such as urinary bladder cancer.
rationales.F11: The presence of a right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation is strongly indicative of nephrolithiasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on imaging, along with hematuria, strongly supports Urinary Bladder Cancer as the most likely diagnosis.
